title: Remove Consecutive Duplicates

concept.title: Build the result and look at its last letter
body: To drop repeated neighbours you can build a new string and add a letter only when it differs from the **last letter of the result so far**. Comparing with the result instead of the input also works when you extend the idea to longer chains.
In Python a list of characters is joined at the end; in Java a `StringBuilder` plays that role, and in C++ a `string` can be appended to directly.

statement: Replace every block of equal neighbouring letters of a word by a single letter. For example `aabbbcaa` becomes `abca`. Equal letters that are not neighbours stay.
inputFormat: A single word of lowercase letters.

examples.note: The second a-block is not next to the first one, so it stays.

hints: Keep a result that you build letter by letter.
Add a letter only if the result is empty or its last letter is different.
Compare with the last letter of the result, not with a letter you have already thrown away.

explanation: A letter is kept only when it differs from the last kept letter.
